title: Phytolith Extraction and Counting Procedure for Modern Plant Material
author: Francesca D’Agostini

steps.title: Dry Plant Tissues
steps.instruction: Dry the collected plant tissues to evaluate biomass and prepare for extraction.

substeps.instruction: Store each sample in a separate paper bag and place them in a dryer (e.g., IWC125 Leec drying cabinet).
Dry at 60-70°C, checking bags daily for fungi infection.
Weigh samples until no weight loss is observed or until tissues become brittle to the touch.

steps.title: Wash Samples in Ultrasound Bath
steps.instruction: Remove extraneous debris from the samples using an ultrasound bath at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Cut samples into pieces to fit into labeled glass beakers (100 ml beakers are sufficient for grasses).
Cover samples with distilled water and place beakers in the ultrasound bath (e.g., Ulsonix Proclean 3.0), ensuring the container is filled without overflowing the beakers.
Wash for 00:05:00.
Remove samples with tweezers and place on aluminum foil to dry.

steps.title: Ash Plant Material
steps.instruction: Mineralize organic material by ashing the plant tissue in a furnace.

substeps.instruction: Weigh approximately 0.1 g of plant material (using a precision scale, e.g., Mettler Toledo MS105DU) into a labeled ceramic crucible.
Cover the crucible with a ceramic or foil lid (non-sealed is acceptable to allow oxygen entry and avoid carbonization).
Place crucibles in the furnace (e.g., Nabertherm C450) and ash at 500ºC for 12:00:00 (including warm-up time).
Allow crucibles to cool completely before removing samples.

steps.title: Digest Carbonates with HCl
steps.instruction: Remove carbonates and remaining organic material using hydrochloric acid.

substeps.instruction: Transfer ashes from the crucible to a 5 ml Eppendorf tube using a clean spatula for each sample.
Add 900 µL of 10% v/v HCl and vortex (e.g., ES714R Maxi Mixer).
Leave to react for 05:00:00 (or until reaction stops) with the tube cap open in a fume cupboard; add more HCl if the sample begins to dry.
Dilute the solution with 450 µL of distilled water.
Screw on the lid and centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 00:05:00 (e.g., Mini Spin Eppendorf®5453).
Discard the supernatant and repeat the dilution and centrifugation process three more times.

steps.title: Oxidize Organic Material with H2O2
steps.instruction: Further oxidize organic material using hydrogen peroxide.

substeps.instruction: Add 900 µL of 10% v/v H₂O₂ to the tube.
Place the tube with the cap open in a dryer or hot bath at 40ºC until the reaction stops (approx. 09:00:00 for chaff/leaves, at least 12 hours for stems).
Every 2 hours, rinse samples with distilled water (dilute with 450 µL water, centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 00:05:00, discard supernatant) and add another 900 μl H₂O₂.
Ensure the sample does not dry by adding more H₂O₂ solution if necessary.
Once the reaction stops, dilute with 450 µL of distilled water, centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 00:05:00, discard supernatant, and repeat this process three more times.

steps.title: Dry and Weigh Silica Extracts
steps.instruction: Dry the resulting silica powder to determine the final weight.

substeps.instruction: Dry extracts in a drying cabinet at 60ºC.
Cool the extracts and weigh them.
Repeat weighing until no weight loss is observed and the powder is loose and clear in color.

steps.title: Prepare Microscope Slides
steps.instruction: Mount the silica powder on slides for observation.

substeps.instruction: Place 0.0001 g of silica powder on a microscope slide using a clean spatula.
Add 4 drops of Entellan New® and gently stir with a micro clean spatula/spoon to distribute phytoliths homogeneously.
Cover with a cover slip (24 x 32 mm or 24 x 24 mm), maintaining consistent size across all slides.
Let the slide dry for at least 30 minutes, though 12:00:00 is suggested for optimal density.

steps.title: Count and Classify Phytoliths
steps.instruction: Identify and quantify phytolith morphotypes using the ICPN 2.0.

substeps.instruction: Observe and rotate phytoliths to inspect tridimensional shape.
Note the number of fields of view observed to calculate concentration based on cover slip size.
Count until 50 skeletons (multi-cell structures) have been numbered and their cells classified.
Separately count and classify all disarticulated phytoliths (single cells/monoliths) found along the pathway.
Summarize data into a unique file to obtain total phytolith size, absolute number of each morphotype, and silica skeleton sizes.
